SMTO-CFG-0062 — SMTO can't start because its shutdown wait time is too low

GUID: 2c6a8ae7-373a-4e2c-9a64-90df14624033
Slug: config-worker-join-timeout-seconds-must-be-greater
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because the time it allows its background work to finish when shutting down is set to zero or less. Your conversations and settings were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find where SMTO is started (the terminal command, a startup script or the service settings) and look for a setting named AOR_WORKER_JOIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. SMTO reads this shutdown wait time from that setting when it starts.
  2. Delete that setting to use the usual 2 seconds, or change it to a positive number of seconds, such as 2. SMTO needs at least a moment to let its background work stop cleanly when it shuts down.
  3. Start SMTO again from the same place where you changed the setting. The new wait time is used from the next start.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't change task time limits or Model timeouts to fix this; they are separate from this shutdown wait.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected worker_join_timeout_seconds (environment variable AOR_WORKER_JOIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) because it is zero or negative.

What this means

  • Effective worker_join_timeout_seconds is zero or negative. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Effective worker_join_timeout_seconds is zero or negative.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the effective join timeout independently of task deadlines.

How to fix it

  • Unset AOR_WORKER_JOIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS or set it to a positive number of seconds (default 2) in the Server's launch environment, then restart; when unset, the already-validated config.yaml runtime.worker_join_timeout_seconds is used. It is the join timeout for the native worker, task queue, scheduler and artifact maintenance threads at shutdown and is unrelated to task deadlines.
  • Set worker_join_timeout_seconds to the intended positive shutdown-wait duration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported positive worker-join timeout validates.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
